svg.title: Coupeville Red Lipstick Special wiring reference
svg.desc: Builder reference in the numbered-panel style of the Relay Arc wiring diagram. It shows the three lipstick pickups with hot, return, and case leads; the series chain from ground through neck, middle, and bridge to the volume input; functional contact maps for the three SPDT enable switches and two DPDT phase switches; the fourteen operating states; rear-view A500K volume and tone pots; the output jack; and the common ground.

g.text: COUPEVILLE RED LIPSTICK SPECIAL • WIRING REFERENCE
SERIES CHAIN • MATCH IDENTICAL BOXED NET LABELS • FUNCTIONAL SWITCH CONTACTS MUST BE METERED
Electrical lead roles, not manufacturer wire colors
NORMAL: hot lead toward volume, return lead toward ground.
NORMAL: hot lead toward volume, return lead toward ground.
NORMAL: hot lead toward volume, return lead toward ground.
ON = pickup between IN and OUT • OFF = IN joined to OUT
All three OFF joins GND to BUS: built-in mute. No pickup coil lead is wired to GND except through the neck enable switch.
UP: COMMON ↔ ON throw. DOWN: COMMON ↔ OFF throw. A DPDT may be used; leave its second pole unconnected.
Functional contacts, not lug numbers: identify the real toggle lugs by continuity (assembly guide §2).
Functional contact map • neck and middle only
Cross-wired: hot lead → NORMAL throw of pole 1 and REVERSE throw of pole 2; return lead → the other two throws.
The two poles never touch. Bridge has no phase switch: it is the fixed reference.
Chain listed ground end first • + NORMAL, − REVERSE
Filled dot = enable switch ON (lever UP). Phase levers of a disabled pickup have no effect.
Relative phase is electrical: confirm acoustic in-phase / out-of-phase for each pair on the bench.
Fed by the series chain output (BUS).
BOTTOM VIEW • solder lugs face the viewer • shaft away
Never mirror this drawing between projects.
BOTTOM VIEW • solder lugs face the viewer • shaft away
No treble bleed • no loading resistors.
No pickup volume or tone controls.
GND = neck enable common (chain start) • each pickup CASE lead • volume CCW lug • 22 nF return • jack sleeve • pot cases • conductive switch chassis • cavity shielding • bridge/string ground.
NO coil lead goes to GND except through E-N. Keep N-OUT, N-Y, N-H, N-R, M-OUT, M-Y, M-H, M-R, B-R and every toggle terminal clear of shielding and ground.
Meter each loose pickup first: the RETURN lead reads the coil resistance to the HOT lead; the CASE lead reads open to hot and continuity to the case. Never wire the case lead into the chain.
With pickups disconnected, meter every enable and phase lever state; in all eight enable states, GND–N-OUT, N-OUT–M-OUT, M-OUT–BUS close only through OFF modules, and N=M=B=OFF joins GND to BUS.
After wiring pickups: DC resistance at the jack = sum of the active pickups (about 0 Ω all OFF). Tap-test all 13 sounding states; confirm each pair’s phase and hum on the bench.
EXPERIMENTAL BENCH DESIGN • lead colors, toggle lugs, and body fit are unverified • identify GFS leads by meter and the supplied documentation, not by color alone.
Netlist check: 887 checks across 32 switch states passed when this sheet was generated.
